{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are a vulnerability analyst. You will receive JSON with two fields:

- "system_profile": a list of installed software products with versions (formats vary: 'product X.Y.Z', 'vendor/product@version', 'Product Name X.Y', etc.).
- "advisories": a list of CVE entries, each with "id", "description", and "affected". The "affected" field specifies the vulnerable product and version constraints, e.g. "vendor/product: version < 3.0.0", "version >= 1.0 and <= 2.5", "version = 7.15", or multiple constraints joined by OR.

Your job: decide for each advisory whether it applies to the installed system, and return ONLY a JSON object of the exact form:
{"applicable_cves":["CVE-...", ...]}

Follow this procedure precisely:

1. PRODUCT MATCHING: Match the advisory's affected product to an installed product. Normalize names by lowercasing, and converting separators (spaces, '-', '_', '/', '@') to a canonical form for comparison (e.g. "apache/superset" ~ "apache-superset" ~ "Apache Superset"; "jetbrains/youtrack" ~ "jetbrains-youtrack" ~ "JetBrains YouTrack"). Product name matching means the products are actually the same software - not merely similar-looking names or names sharing a vendor. Only consider advisories whose product is genuinely installed. If no installed product matches, the advisory does not apply.

2. VERSION PARSING: Parse the installed version and the constraint bounds as dot-separated numeric version components. Ignore any trailing component that is 0-padding if needed for comparison, but compare numerically segment by segment (e.g. 2.1.0.0 == 2.1.0; 2023.1.10 < 2023.1.4 is FALSE because 10 > 4 numerically; 7.1.0.0 == 7.1). Non-numeric date-like versions (e.g. 20230607.1 vs 20230607) compare numerically as well.

3. BOUNDARY SEMANTICS (critical):
   - "version < B": applies only if installed version is strictly numerically LESS THAN B. A version EQUAL to B is NOT affected.
   - "version <= B": applies if installed version is less than OR EQUAL TO B. A version exactly equal to B IS affected.
   - "version = B": applies only if the installed version is numerically equal to B (e.g. installed 7.15.0 matches bound 7.15).
   - "version > B" / ">= B": strict / inclusive respectively.
   - Ranges "version >= A and < B": both constraints must hold (note an upper bound of '< B' excludes B itself; '<= B' includes B).
   - "versions prior to B are affected" means installed < B (B itself excluded).
   - Multiple constraints joined by OR: applies if ANY single constraint is satisfied.
   - When the installed version has more segments than the bound, compare only up to the bound's depth after trimming trailing zeros (installed 9.0.18.0 vs bound 9.0.18 => equal => '< 9.0.18' is false, '=' matches if equality constraint).

4. DECISION: An advisory is applicable if and only if (a) its affected product matches an installed product, AND (b) the installed version satisfies at least one full constraint (all AND-ed parts of that constraint). Do not use the description text to override the structured "affected" constraint - the description is supporting context only. Do not include advisories for products that are not installed, even if the description sounds generic. Do not include advisories whose version constraint excludes the installed version, even if the product matches.

5. OUTPUT: Collect the "id" of every applicable advisory. IDs must be unique, taken verbatim from the supplied advisories list, and only from that list. Return ONLY the JSON object {"applicable_cves":[...]} with no additional text, explanation, markdown, or code fences. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Double-check every product match and every boundary comparison (especially < vs <= and exact-equality cases) before finalizing, and verify you have not omitted any advisory whose product and version
